lead.headline: Sea Robin pipeline's 2025 gas-loss reports reuse one number, 1,587,069, whole, halved and split three ways
lead.number: 1,587,069 filed whole (May 17), as two 793,534 halves (Jan 13) and, minus 3,508, as three 527,853 blowdowns; counted once, 2025 is still the record at about 3.5M vs 2.98M in 2022.
lead.watch_out: No unit column: if Sea Robin typed cubic feet instead of thousand cubic feet, 2025 falls to about 1.94M, an ordinary year.

sources.quote: Pipeline mishaps unintentionally released nearly 9.7 billion cubic feet of gas into the atmosphere between 2019 and late 2023, according to a Reuters examination of incident report data maintained by the U.S. Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA).
sources.page_context: eline leaks – caused by things like punctures, corrosion, severe weather and faulty equipment – happen routinely and are a climate menace that is not currently counted in the official U.S. tally of greenhouse gas emissions, according to a Reuters examination of public data and regulatory documents. Pipeline mishaps unintentionally released nearly 9.7 billion cubic feet of gas into the atmosphere between 2019 and late 2023, according to a Reuters examination of incident report data maintained by the U.S. Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA). That is the climate equivalent of running four average-sized coal-fired power plants for a year, according to an Environmental Defense Fund (EDF) online calculator.
